messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — ran the warmup scarcity profile this morning across three prod-like hosts. seeing sustained low prefix hit rate for long-tail prompts during high-concurrency bursts; kernel choice seems fine but cache pressure is killing warmup.

matt: can you paste the numbers?

elaine: sure — baseline run (no taper): avg hit-rate 61.8% over first 15m, median latency +18% on 95th under 500qps, GPU cache footprint 4.2GB -> ramp to 6.9GB before OOM mitigation triggered. KV fragmentation visible in slab stats.

sam: that matches the flamegraphs i looked at. a lot of small allocations from prompt canonicalization path, then LRU churn.

elaine: proposal: introduce "TTL taper" — shortest TTL on insert (e.g., 30s) when memory pressure high, then progressively increase TTL for surviving keys (60s -> 180s -> pinned-ish) as the slab compaction rate improves and hit-rate justifies retention. taper decision driven by two signals: live memory utilization and observed prefix re-access rate.

hao: interesting. how is this different from existing adaptive-ttl? we already do ttl-extension on hits, right?

elaine: yes, existing is hit-based extension only. taper adds proactive increase on cohort-level signals so warmup keys that are getting reused quickly don't get evicted just because initial global pressure spikes. prevents oscillation when batch routing picks suboptimal kernel and briefly starves cache.

irene: curious about kernel selection interplay — do we mark keys with kernel-meta so fallback routes don't cause double-inserts?

matt: we should. suggestion: attach a small tag to cache key metadata: kernel_hint and sequence_len_bucket. when routing falls back to cheaper kernel, we can avoid re-inserting identical prefix with new kernel tag, instead update metadata. reduces dup keys and fragmentation.

elaine: agree. here's the quick config snippet i tested (pseudo):

```
cache.ttl.taper: [30, 60, 180]  # seconds
cache.ttl.taper_thresholds: [0.9, 0.6]  # reaccess ratio thresholds to move to next TTL
cache.taper.memory_high: 0.88  # don't expand TTL if memory > 88%
cache.meta.attach: [kernel_hint, seq_bucket]
```

sam: results?

elaine: 10m A/B: taper enabled -> initial 15m hit-rate jumped 61.8% -> 74.1%, 95th latency dropped ~12%. GPU resident stayed flatter: 5.1GB peak vs 6.9GB. fragmentation metric (slab small-chunk %) improved by ~9pp. no new OOMs in 2 stress runs.

hao: nice. any regressions with batching? we sometimes see larger batches causing longer tail latency if TTL extends keys and increases coalescing.

elaine: observed a micro-regression on tail in one workload: when taper kept many small prefixes, batching logic spent extra time coalescing KV requests. fixed by updating batching heuristic to cap coalesce window for small-key cohorts. small change: if cohort_key_count > 2048 and avg_key_len < 64 then coalesce_window_ms = min(2, default).

matt: will that affect throughput?

elaine: negligible throughput loss in perf tests, but 95/99 latency improved overall once cap in place.

irene: how safe is deployment? can we toggle taper per-pool/region?

elaine: yes, rollout plan: config flag per-pool, start with shadow traffic in us-west-1, then 10% canary (read-only), then 50% canary, observe hit-rate, latency, slab fragmentation, kernel path churn. fallback toggle if memory > 94% or OOM event. deploy-bot: can you schedule a canary deploy window tomorrow 02:00 UTC?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary for 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC, 3 hosts in us-west-1 pool. will emit events to #incidents if oom or >2% error rate spike.

sam: action items?

matt: 1) irene to add kernel_hint and seq_bucket to cache key schema (PR 1).
2) sam to add coalesce cap heuristic (PR 2).
3) elaine to push taper config and rollout plan (PR 3 + canary manifest).
4) run 6h soak and gather slab/frag/oom telemetry.

elaine: I'll do the telemetry dashboard and post numbers after 6h soak. thanks all. :thumbsup:

hao: if taper looks good we should bake it into default mixing policy for dedicated pools.

elaine: agreed — will write up short RFC depending on canary results.
